attrs.label: B2B content has a harder job
attrs.html:
B2B content has a harder job

Fewer buyers, bigger deals and longer decisions. Pick a challenge to see how we handle it.

The challengeBuyers research for months, and most of it happens before they ever contact you. If you’re not in that research, you’re not on the shortlist.

Our approach

Be useful at every stage of a long decision, not just at the end.

Most of a B2B purchase happens before anyone talks to you. Buyers read, compare and ask colleagues for months. We make sure that whenever they look, they find something useful from you.

In practice

  • A map of the questions buyers ask in month 1, month 3 and month 6
  • At least one strong piece for every stage, not just “book a demo” pages
  • Emails that send the next useful piece as a lead moves forward
  • Older pieces updated, so they keep working for years

Why it matters

Companies that show up early make the shortlist. Companies that only show up at the end compete on price.

Methods we use

  1. 1Buyer journey map

    The questions buyers ask at each stage, from sales calls and search data.

  2. 2Content for every stage

    Guides for early research, comparisons for the shortlist, proof for the final call.

  3. 3Nurture sequences

    Emails that send the right piece as a lead moves forward.

  4. 4Regular refreshes

    Older pieces kept accurate, so they keep working for years.

What you get

  • A journey map
  • A 12-month content calendar
  • Nurture emails

The challengeSix or more people sign off a typical purchase. The CFO, IT, legal and the people who’ll use it all ask different questions.

Our approach

Give every person in the room the answers they need, in their language.

A typical B2B purchase needs six or more people to agree. Each one has different worries, and your champion has to convince all of them. We give your champion the answers to pass around.

In practice

  • We learn who signs off from your sales team and recent deals
  • Separate pieces for finance, IT, operations and day-to-day users
  • A buyer’s guide your champion can forward to the whole group
  • Sales kits that bundle the right pieces for each person

Why it matters

Deals stall when one person on the committee has an unanswered question. Content answers it before it slows the deal.

Methods we use

  1. 1Role mapping

    We interview your sales team to learn who signs off and what each person worries about.

  2. 2Pieces for each role

    A business case for finance, security and integration answers for IT, how-tos for users.

  3. 3A shareable buyer’s guide

    One document your champion can pass around the committee.

  4. 4Sales kits by role

    The right pieces bundled for each person your sales team meets.

What you get

  • Role-by-role content map
  • A buyer’s guide
  • Sales kits

The challengeYour best material lives with busy partners, engineers and founders who never have time to write.

Our approach

Capture what your experts know, without taking their week.

Your partners, engineers and founders know more than any writer. They just don’t have time to write. We take 30 minutes of their time and do the rest.

In practice

  • One short interview a month per expert, recorded and transcribed
  • A specialist writer turns each call into an article and LinkedIn posts
  • Your expert reviews a near-final draft once, usually in 15 minutes
  • Everything is published under their name, with an author page

Why it matters

Buyers trust people more than brands. Content from named experts gets read, shared and remembered.

Methods we use

  1. 130-minute interviews

    One short call a month per expert, recorded and transcribed.

  2. 2Written in their voice

    Our writers turn each call into articles and posts that sound like them.

  3. 3One review, not five

    Your expert checks a near-final draft once, usually in 15 minutes.

  4. 4Content for their profiles

    LinkedIn posts under their name, so their ideas travel further.

What you get

  • Monthly expert articles
  • LinkedIn posts for your leaders
  • An interview calendar

The challengeWhat you sell is hard to explain in a sentence, and generic copy makes it sound like everyone else.

Our approach

Explain complicated offerings clearly, without dumbing them down.

If your product takes ten minutes to explain, most websites lose the buyer in the first one. We explain it clearly, step by step, without making it sound simple-minded.

In practice

  • Writers who already know your field, briefed by your technical team
  • How-it-works guides with diagrams your designers can polish
  • A glossary of the terms your buyers search for
  • A technical review of every piece before it goes live

Why it matters

Buyers don’t shortlist what they don’t understand. Clear content shortens the time to “I get it”.

Methods we use

  1. 1Specialist writers

    Writers who already know your field, briefed by your technical team.

  2. 2Explainers and diagrams

    How it works, step by step, with visuals your designers can polish.

  3. 3Plain-language glossary

    The terms your buyers search for, explained simply.

  4. 4Technical review

    Every piece checked by someone who knows the product.

What you get

  • How-it-works guides
  • Diagrams and explainers
  • A glossary

The challengeCompetitors publish the same “ultimate guides”. Buyers can’t tell you apart, so they choose on price.

Our approach

Give buyers a reason to remember you: a clear point of view.

When every company in your market publishes the same “ultimate guide”, buyers can’t tell you apart. A clear point of view gives them a reason to remember you.

In practice

  • A two-hour workshop with your leaders to agree what you believe
  • Original research that only you can publish
  • Opinion articles that take a side, written with your experts
  • A review of what competitors cover badly, so you can own those topics

Why it matters

Buyers remember a strong opinion long after they’ve forgotten a generic guide.

Methods we use

  1. 1Point-of-view workshop

    Two hours with your leaders to agree what you believe that others don’t.

  2. 2Original research

    Surveys and data only you have, which journalists and AI tools quote.

  3. 3Opinion pieces

    Articles that take a side, written with your experts.

  4. 4Content gap review

    What competitors cover badly, and where you can own the topic.

What you get

  • Your point of view, written down
  • An annual research report
  • Opinion articles

The challengeMarketing publishes content sales never uses, and sales writes its own one-pagers in a hurry.

Our approach

Make content your sales team actually reaches for.

Marketing often creates content sales never uses, while sales writes its own one-pagers late at night. We build content with your sales team, for the calls they actually have.

In practice

  • Interviews with your sales team about the questions and objections they hear
  • Pieces that answer the hard questions before buyers ask them
  • A sales library sorted by deal stage and buyer role
  • Ready-to-send follow-up emails with the right piece attached

Why it matters

Content that sales uses keeps deals moving between meetings, without another call.

Methods we use

  1. 1Sales interviews

    We learn the objections and questions that come up on every call.

  2. 2Objection-handling content

    Pieces that answer the hard questions before the buyer asks.

  3. 3A sales content library

    Everything in one place, sorted by stage and role.

  4. 4Follow-up emails

    Ready-to-send emails with the right piece attached.

What you get

  • One-pagers and battle cards
  • A sales library
  • Follow-up email templates

The challengeContent rarely gets credit for deals, so when budgets get tight it’s the first thing cut.

Our approach

Show which pieces your deals read, in your own CRM.

Content rarely gets credit for deals, because nobody tracks it. We connect what buyers read to the deals in your CRM, so you can see what content is worth.

In practice

  • Content views connected to contacts and deals in HubSpot or Salesforce
  • A list of which pieces each won deal read before it closed
  • A monthly report on readers, leads and pipeline, in plain English
  • Quarterly reviews of what worked and where to spend next

Why it matters

When you can show the pipeline content influenced, the budget stops being the first thing cut.

Methods we use

  1. 1CRM tracking

    Content views connected to contacts and deals in HubSpot or Salesforce.

  2. 2Pipeline by piece

    Which pieces each won deal read before it closed.

  3. 3A monthly report

    Readers, leads and pipeline, in plain English.

  4. 4Quarterly reviews

    What worked, what didn’t and where to spend next.

What you get

  • Content attribution in your CRM
  • A monthly pipeline report
  • Quarterly reviews

attrs.lead: Can’t find your answer? Ask us on a free 30-minute call.

items.question: What is B2B content marketing?
items.answer: B2B content marketing is creating useful content, such as guides, research, case studies and thought leadership, that helps business buyers through long research and decision processes, so they choose you.

items.question: What does a B2B content marketing agency do?
items.answer: It researches your buyers, plans content for every stage of the sale, interviews your experts, writes and edits the content, distributes it and reports on the pipeline it influences.

items.question: How is B2B content marketing different from B2C?
items.answer: B2B buyers are fewer, deals are bigger and several people decide. Content has to answer detailed questions for each of them, over a much longer time.

items.question: How much do B2B content marketing services cost?
items.answer: Every programme is a fixed monthly price, based on how much content you need and how specialist it is. We quote after a free 30-minute call.

items.question: How do you measure B2B content marketing?
items.answer: We track readers, leads and, through your CRM, which pieces each deal read before it closed.

items.question: Do you use AI to write content?
items.answer: No. Every piece is written and edited by people. We use AI only for research.
